```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Tseng 2025 builds a theoretical quantitative systems pharmacology model of the
circadian clock in a lung cell and couples it to SARS-CoV-2 infection. The
clock drives the viral entry receptor ACE2 (through CLOCK:BMAL1) and represses
interferon-stimulated genes (ISG), so the infection oscillates with the clock.
The REV-ERB agonist SR9009, which represses *Bmal1* through REV-ERB, is then
given as a once-daily 1 h exposure at different circadian times to look for a
dosing time that suppresses the virus while keeping the clock running.

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tseng_2025_SR9009_qsp"))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13277>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11812942/>

The equations are printed in Data S1 and the parameter values in Table S1. The
author also deposited the CellDesigner model in SBML (File S1), which carries
the initial conditions, the virus-entry rate `kin_Vfree`, and the event
switches used for the inoculation, the SR9009 doses and the cortisol pulses;
two Python scripts (robustness and sensitivity analysis) run a reduced copy of
that SBML file.

# Population

There is no study population. The model is a single in silico lung epithelial
cell, with all levels in arbitrary units and time in hours. The mRNA
degradation rates were taken from experimental data or published models and
the remaining parameters and initial conditions were tuned by hand until the
clock oscillated with a 24 h period and the mRNA peak phases fell in the
experimental windows of Figure 2b. The infection layer was matched
qualitatively to the BMAL1 / ACE2 / ISG findings of Zhuang et al. (2021) in
Calu-3 lung epithelial cells. SR9009 has no pharmacokinetic model: its exposure
is the on/off level of a term added to *Rev-Erb* transcription.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tseng_2025_SR9009_qsp")()$population`.

# How the model is driven

Three inputs are given as events, each on its own state:

| Input | State | On | Off |
|---|---|---|---|
| SARS-CoV-2 inoculation | `vfree` | dose `amt = 1` | (stays on) |
| SR9009 exposure | `sr9009` | dose `amt = 1` | replacement `evid = 5, amt = 0` |
| Cortisol pulse | `cortisol` | dose `amt = 1` | replacement `evid = 5, amt = 0` |

The SBML file does the same thing with event assignments: `Vfree` is set to 1
at 24 h, `Ka_rev_SR9009` is switched between 0 and 0.5, and the cortisol
parameters between their resting and pulse values. Circadian time (CT) is the
model time modulo 24 h: Figure 5 states that SR9009 at CT 18 starts at 66 h.

```{r helpers}
# Observation grid on an ODE state; the algebraic outputs (total_virus) are
# returned as columns at every observation row.
obs_grid <- function(end = 200, by = 0.1) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, end, by = by), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "pc_mrna")
}

# Inoculation at 24 h (File S1 'Virus_on': T_virus_on = 24, Vfree_on = 1).
inoculate <- function(time = 24) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = time, evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = "vfree")
}

# A switch held on from `on` to `on + dur` for each start time.
pulse <- function(cmt, on, dur = 1) {
  rbind(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = on, evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = cmt),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = on + dur, evid = 5L, amt = 0, cmt = cmt)
  )
}

solve_events <- function(model, ev, ...) {
  ev <- dplyr::arrange(ev, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10, ...))
}

# Local maxima / minima of a sampled curve.
peaks <- function(t, x) {
  i <- which(diff(sign(diff(x))) == -2) + 1
  data.frame(time = t[i], value = x[i])
}
troughs <- function(t, x) {
  i <- which(diff(sign(diff(x))) == 2) + 1
  data.frame(time = t[i], value = x[i])
}
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Source location |
|---|---|
| Clock mRNA ODEs (`cb_mrna`, `pc_mrna`, `dbp_mrna`, `ror_mrna`, `rev_mrna`) | Data S1 Eqs. 1-5; SBML reactions re10, re44, re40, re22, re21 |
| Clock protein and complex ODEs | Data S1 Eqs. 6-12 |
| ACE2, endosomal virus, replicated virus, ISG ODEs | Data S1 Eqs. 13-16 |
| Free virus as a non-depleted input | Data S1 (four ODEs added; `[Vfree]` appears only as a driver); Figure 5a |
| Transcription, translation, complex-formation, threshold, Hill and degradation constants | Table S1 |
| `kin_vfree` = 0.3 | File S1 (SBML global parameter `kin_Vfree`; absent from Table S1) |
| `ace2_mrna` = 1, `isg_pre` = 1 | File S1 (boundary species `ace2_RNA`, `ISGpre`) |
| `ka_rev_sr9009` = 0.5, 1 h per dose | File S1 (`Ka_rev_SR9009_on` = 0.5, `SP` = 1); Figure 5b right axis; Results text |
| `kact_pc_cortisol` = 10, `krep_rev_cortisol` = 0, 1 h pulse | Methods 'Modeling cortisol pulses'; File S1 (`kact_pc_cortisol_on`, `Krep_rev_cortisol_on`, `CP` = 1) |
| Initial conditions of the 14 clock / infection states | File S1 (species `initialAmount`) |
| `total_virus = vendo + vrep` | File S1 assignment rule `total_virus`; plotted as 'SARS-CoV-2' in Figure 5 and 'Total Virus' in Figure S8 |

The parameter values are checked against a transcription of Table S1 (and of

# Free-running clock (Figure 2)

```{r clock}
sim_clock <- solve_events(mod, obs_grid(end = 200, by = 0.01))

clock_long <- sim_clock |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 50) |>
  dplyr::select(time, cb = cb_mrna, Dbp = dbp_mrna, pc = pc_mrna, `Rev-Erb` = rev_mrna, Ror = ror_mrna) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "mRNA", values_to = "level")
```

```{r fig2a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2a of Tseng 2025: clock mRNA oscillations of the free-running model."}
ggplot(clock_long, aes(time, level, colour = mRNA)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "RNA level (a.u.)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 2b compares the simulated peak time of each mRNA (black dots) with the
window in which the measured mRNA is above 70% of its peak (colour bands,
read from the figure). The simulated peaks are taken from the fifth cycle so
that they are on the limit cycle:

```{r fig2b}
peak_ct <- function(x) {
  p <- peaks(sim_clock$time, x)
  p <- p[p$time >= 96 & p$time < 120, ]
  p$time[1] %% 24
}
phase <- tibble::tibble(
  mRNA = c("Bmal (cb)", "Dbp", "Per2 (pc)", "Rora", "Rev"),
  sim_ct = c(
    peak_ct(sim_clock$cb_mrna), peak_ct(sim_clock$dbp_mrna),
    peak_ct(sim_clock$pc_mrna), peak_ct(sim_clock$ror_mrna),
    peak_ct(sim_clock$rev_mrna)
  ),
  # Figure 2b: shaded CT cells (window start, window end + 1 h) and the
  # simulated peak dot, read by the maintainers.
  window_lo = c(0, 8, 11, 8, 8),
  window_hi = c(3, 14, 17, 21, 14),
  paper_dot = c(2, 9, 15, 15, 8)
)
phase |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_ct = round(sim_ct, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "mRNA" = mRNA, "Simulated peak (CT, h)" = sim_ct,
    "Window start (CT)" = window_lo, "Window end (CT)" = window_hi,
    "Figure 2b dot (CT)" = paper_dot
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Peak phases of the clock mRNAs against Figure 2b.")
stopifnot(
  all(phase$sim_ct >= phase$window_lo & phase$sim_ct < phase$window_hi),
  all(abs(phase$sim_ct - phase$paper_dot) < 1)
)
```

The state at the start of the simulation is a point on the limit cycle, so the
oscillation neither decays nor grows and the model returns to the same state
one period later:

```{r limit-cycle}
pk_pc <- peaks(sim_clock$time, sim_clock$pc_mrna)
period <- diff(pk_pc$time)
amp <- range(pk_pc$value)
c(min_period = min(period), max_period = max(period), min_peak = amp[1], max_peak = amp[2])
stopifnot(all(abs(period - 24) < 0.1), diff(amp) < 1e-3)
```

# Sensitivity of period and amplitude (Figures S3-S4)

The paper reports local response coefficients from a 3% perturbation of each
parameter, averaged over the increase and the decrease, with the period and
amplitude of `pc_RNA` taken from a 200 h simulation sampled every 0.005 h
(the deposited script `PSP-2024-0047-s06.py`). The period is the mean of the
last two peak-to-peak intervals and the amplitude is the last peak minus the
trough before it. Four of the coefficients are quoted in the Results text.

```{r sensitivity}
clock_metrics <- function(params) {
  s <- solve_events(mod, obs_grid(end = 200, by = 0.005), params = params)
  p <- peaks(s$time, s$pc_mrna)
  n <- nrow(p)
  period <- mean(diff(p$time)[(n - 2):(n - 1)])
  last <- s$time >= p$time[n - 1] & s$time <= p$time[n]
  amplitude <- p$value[n] - min(s$pc_mrna[last])
  c(period = period, amplitude = amplitude)
}
base_metrics <- clock_metrics(theta)
response_coefficient <- function(par, delta = 0.03) {
  up <- theta
  up[[par]] <- up[[par]] * (1 + delta)
  dn <- theta
  dn[[par]] <- dn[[par]] * (1 - delta)
  ((clock_metrics(up) - base_metrics) / base_metrics / delta +
    (clock_metrics(dn) - base_metrics) / base_metrics / (-delta)) / 2
}
rc_check <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("kdeg_cb_mrna", "kdeg_cbc", "ktx_ror", "ktl_ror"),
  paper_name = c("kd_cb", "kd_CBC", "k_ror", "k_ROR"),
  output = c("period", "period", "amplitude", "amplitude"),
  paper_rc = c(-0.262, -0.274, 3.22, 3.22)
)
rc_check$sim_rc <- mapply(
  function(p, o) response_coefficient(p)[[o]],
  rc_check$parameter, rc_check$output
)
rc_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_rc = round(sim_rc, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Paper name" = paper_name, "Output" = output,
    "Paper RC" = paper_rc, "Simulated RC" = sim_rc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Response coefficients quoted in the Results against the model.")
stopifnot(abs(rc_check$sim_rc - rc_check$paper_rc) < 0.01)
```

# Cortisol phase-response curve (Figure 3)

A 1 h cortisol pulse raises *Per/Cry* transcription by 10 and switches off
*Rev-Erb* transcription. Each pulse is given on the third simulated day at
circadian times 0-24 in 4 h steps, and the phase shift is the advance of the
`pc_RNA` peak between 200 and 225 h relative to the unperturbed clock (positive
= advance).

```{r prc}
prc_peak <- function(s) {
  p <- peaks(s$time, s$pc_mrna)
  p$time[p$time > 200 & p$time < 225][1]
}
grid_prc <- obs_grid(end = 240, by = 0.01)
peak_free <- prc_peak(solve_events(mod, grid_prc))
prc <- tibble::tibble(
  ct = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
  # Figure 3 open circles, read by the maintainers (h).
  paper_shift = c(-1.5, 8.8, 2.0, -1.4, -2.7, -1.8, -1.4)
)
prc$sim_shift <- vapply(prc$ct, function(ct) {
  s <- solve_events(mod, rbind(pulse("cortisol", 48 + ct), grid_prc))
  shift <- peak_free - prc_peak(s)
  ((shift + 12) %% 24) - 12
}, numeric(1))
```

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Tseng 2025: phase-response curve to 1 h cortisol pulses. Line and filled points = model; open circles = Figure 3."}
ggplot(prc, aes(ct)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_shift), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = sim_shift)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = paper_shift), shape = 1, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Circadian time (h)", y = "Phase shift (h)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r prc-table}
prc |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_shift = round(sim_shift, 2), diff = round(sim_shift - paper_shift, 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Pulse CT (h)" = ct, "Figure 3 shift (h)" = paper_shift,
    "Simulated shift (h)" = sim_shift, "Difference (h)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Cortisol phase shifts against Figure 3.")
stopifnot(abs(prc$sim_shift - prc$paper_shift) < 0.5)
```

The largest advance follows a pulse in the early subjective morning (CT 4),
as the paper reports.

# Infection without treatment (Figure 5a)

```{r infection}
sim_inf <- solve_events(mod, rbind(inoculate(), obs_grid()))
inf_long <- sim_inf |>
  dplyr::select(
    time, `SARS-CoV-2` = total_virus, `Per and Cry mRNAs` = pc_mrna,
    ACE2 = ace2, ISG = isg, cb_RNA = cb_mrna, rev_RNA = rev_mrna
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "species", values_to = "level")
```

```{r fig5a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5a of Tseng 2025: infection starting at 24 h, no SR9009."}
ggplot(inf_long, aes(time, level, colour = species)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Relative level (a.u.)", colour = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2)) +
  theme_bw()
```

The clock, ACE2 and ISG traces reproduce Figure 5a (for example `pc_RNA`
peaks of 0.89 every 24 h, ACE2 between about 0.4 and 0.8, ISG between about
0.6 and 0.9). The viral load oscillates with a 24 h period and its peaks fall within about
1.5 h of the figure's, but it is lower and its trough comes about 3.5 h
earlier than in the figure:

```{r virus-level}
vir_pk <- peaks(sim_inf$time, sim_inf$total_virus)
vir_tr <- troughs(sim_inf$time, sim_inf$total_virus)
virus_check <- tibble::tibble(
  feature = c("first peak", "first trough"),
  # Figure 5a / Figure S8 'SARS-CoV-2', read by the maintainers.
  paper_time = c(39, 51),
  paper_level = c(1.55, 0.93),
  sim_time = c(vir_pk$time[1], vir_tr$time[1]),
  sim_level = c(vir_pk$value[1], vir_tr$value[1])
)
virus_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = round(paper_level / sim_level, 2), sim_level = round(sim_level, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Feature" = feature, "Figure time (h)" = paper_time,
    "Figure level (a.u.)" = paper_level, "Model time (h)" = sim_time,
    "Model level (a.u.)" = sim_level, "Figure / model" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Viral load after inoculation at 24 h against Figure 5a.")
stopifnot(
  abs(virus_check$sim_time[1] - virus_check$paper_time[1]) < 2,
  all(abs(diff(vir_pk$time[2:5]) - 24) < 0.5)
)
```

The published viral load is about 2.4-fold higher than the deposited
parameters give; see *Assumptions and deviations*.

## The deposited SBML reading: free virus consumed by entry

In File S1 the free virus is an ordinary reactant of the entry reaction, so a
standard SBML simulator depletes it after the single inoculation event. That
reading gives a transient infection that is gone within two days, which is
not what Figure 5a shows:

```{r sbml-literal}
mod_sbml <- mod |> rxode2::model(d / dt(vfree) <- -virus_entry)
sim_sbml <- solve_events(mod_sbml, rbind(inoculate(), obs_grid()))
sim_sbml |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(30, 40, 50, 75, 100)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, vfree, total_virus) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-time, ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Free virus" = vfree, "Total virus" = total_virus) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Free virus depleted by entry (SBML reaction semantics).")
stopifnot(sim_sbml$total_virus[sim_sbml$time == 100] < 1e-4)
```

# SR9009 at CT 18 (Figure 5b)

SR9009 is switched on for 1 h once a day for five days, starting at CT 18 of
the day after inoculation (66 h).

```{r sr9009}
sr_on <- 66 + 24 * (0:4)
sim_sr <- solve_events(mod, rbind(inoculate(), pulse("sr9009", sr_on), obs_grid(by = 0.05)))
sr_long <- sim_sr |>
  dplyr::mutate(Ka_rev_SR9009 = mod$theta[["ka_rev_sr9009"]] * sr9009) |>
  dplyr::select(
    time, `SARS-CoV-2` = total_virus, `Per and Cry mRNAs` = pc_mrna,
    ACE2 = ace2, ISG = isg, cb_RNA = cb_mrna, rev_RNA = rev_mrna, Ka_rev_SR9009
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "species", values_to = "level")
```

```{r fig5b, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5b of Tseng 2025: SR9009 once daily for 1 h starting at CT 18 (66 h)."}
ggplot(sr_long, aes(time, level, colour = species)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Relative level (a.u.)", colour = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2)) +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure S8 plots `pc_RNA` for the same schedule. The SR9009 pulses delay the
clock and deepen the `pc_RNA` trough, and the peaks recover over the five days;
the model reproduces the figure's peaks:

```{r fig-s8-peaks}
pc_sr <- peaks(sim_sr$time, sim_sr$pc_mrna)
pc_sr <- pc_sr[pc_sr$time > 80, ]
s8 <- tibble::tibble(
  cycle = 1:5,
  # Figure S8 'pc_RNA (CT 18)' peaks, read by the maintainers.
  paper_time = c(90, 115, 140, 165, 190),
  paper_peak = c(0.65, 0.66, 0.70, 0.74, 0.78),
  sim_time = pc_sr$time[1:5],
  sim_peak = pc_sr$value[1:5]
)
s8 |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_peak = round(sim_peak, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cycle" = cycle, "Figure S8 time (h)" = paper_time,
    "Figure S8 peak" = paper_peak, "Model time (h)" = sim_time,
    "Model peak" = sim_peak
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "pc_RNA peaks under SR9009 at CT 18 against Figure S8.")
stopifnot(
  abs(s8$sim_time - s8$paper_time) < 1.5,
  abs(s8$sim_peak - s8$paper_peak) < 0.03
)
```

# Dosing time (Figure S8)

The paper repeats the five-day course at circadian times 0-24 in 2 h steps
and reports CT 18 as the time with the strongest viral repression. With the
deposited parameters the viral load at the end of the simulation (200 h) is
also lowest after CT 18 dosing:

```{r ct-sweep}
ct_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 2)
sweep <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ct_grid, function(ct) {
  s <- solve_events(mod, rbind(inoculate(), pulse("sr9009", 48 + ct + 24 * (0:4)), obs_grid()))
  tibble::tibble(ct = ct, time = s$time, total_virus = s$total_virus, pc_mrna = s$pc_mrna)
}))
sweep_end <- sweep |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 200) |>
  dplyr::select(ct, total_virus)
sweep_end |>
  dplyr::mutate(total_virus = round(total_virus, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dosing CT (h)" = ct, "Total virus at 200 h (a.u.)" = total_virus) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Viral load at 200 h after a five-day SR9009 course started at each circadian time.")
stopifnot(sweep_end$ct[which.min(sweep_end$total_virus)] == 18)
```

```{r fig-s8, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure S8 of Tseng 2025: total virus and pc_RNA for SR9009 courses started at CT 0-24; CT 18 highlighted."}
sweep |>
  dplyr::mutate(highlight = ct == 18) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(total_virus, pc_mrna), names_to = "output", values_to = "level") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, level, group = interaction(ct, output), colour = output, alpha = highlight)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.25, `TRUE` = 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Relative level (a.u.)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The drug's antiviral effect is much smaller in the model than in the paper:
the viral load at 200 h after CT 18 dosing is
`r round(100 * (1 - min(sweep_end$total_virus) / sim_inf$total_virus[sim_inf$time == 200]))`%
below the untreated value, whereas Figure S8 shows the CT 18 curve falling to
roughly a fifth of its pre-treatment peaks over the five days.

# PKNCA

Not applicable: the model has no drug concentration. SR9009 is represented
only by the level of a switched transcription term, and the outputs are
relative mRNA, protein and virus levels in arbitrary units. The clock is
instead checked against its period, phases, response coefficients and
phase-response curve above.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Free virus is not consumed by entry.** Data S1 adds four ODEs for the
  infection (ACE2, endosomal virus, replicated virus, ISG) and uses `[Vfree]`
  only as a driver of entry, and Figure 5a shows a sustained, rhythmic
  infection. The SBML File S1, simulated with standard reaction semantics,
  instead consumes free virus, which clears the infection within two days.
  The packaged model follows the printed equations; the SBML reading is shown
  above with `rxode2::model()`.
- **Viral load is lower than published, and SR9009 suppresses it less.** With
  the Table S1 / File S1 parameters the viral load peaks at about 0.63 a.u.
  instead of the 1.55 a.u. of Figure 5a (peaks within about 1.5 h of the
  figure's, same 24 h rhythm), and the five-day CT 18 course lowers it by
  about 30% rather than the roughly five-fold fall of Figure S8. The clock
  under SR9009 matches Figure S8 closely, so the difference lies in the virus
  layer. Neither reading of the free virus reproduces the published viral
  level, and the parameters have not been adjusted to match the figure. The
  paper's viral-load response coefficients (for example `kd_Vendo` = -2.629)
  are not reproduced either. The deposited sensitivity script never resets
  the model between its simulations, so each perturbed run starts from the
  end state of the previous one; that changes a transient output such as the
  peak viral load, but not the period and amplitude of a limit cycle, and
  those coefficients are reproduced exactly.
- **SR9009 schedule and size.** The Methods describe a 4 h exposure started at
  CT 0 with `Ka_rev_SR9009` raised from 0 to 1. The Results, Figure 5b
  (pulses of 0.5 on the right axis) and File S1 (`Ka_rev_SR9009_on` = 0.5,
  `SP` = 1 h) agree on a 1 h exposure of 0.5, and that is what reproduces
  Figure S8; the packaged value is 0.5 and the vignette gives 1 h doses.
- **SR9009 has no pharmacokinetics.** The dose is the on/off level of the
  `Ka_rev_SR9009` term, as in the paper. A dose level other than 1 scales the
  term linearly, which the paper did not explore.
- **Unused SBML elements omitted.** File S1 also contains a KL001 arm whose
  on and off values are identical (`Krep_dPC_KL001` 1 -> 1, `Ki_ACE2_PCC`
  2.4 -> 2.4), dummy gene species consumed by transcription that no rate
  depends on, and bookkeeping events that record the period and amplitude.
  None of these changes any trajectory and none is in the paper, so they are
  not part of the packaged model.
- **Labels in Table S1.** Table S1 lists `Ka_ACE2_CB` and `Ka_ISG_PC` and
  labels `k_ISG` 'Virus production rate'; the SBML file and Data S1 show these
  are the CLOCK:BMAL1 threshold on ACE2, the PER:CRY threshold on ISG, and
  the ISG production rate. Data S1 Eq. 5 prints `H_rev_CB` for `H_rev_CBC`.
- **Fixed parameters.** Only the five mRNA degradation rates, which the
  Methods say were taken from experimental data or published models, and the
  two constant boundary levels (`ace2_mrna`, `isg_pre`) are marked
  `fixed()`. Every other value was tuned by hand rather than estimated; no
  parameter carries an uncertainty.
- **Digitised targets.** The Figure 2b windows, the Figure 3 phase shifts,
  the Figure 5a viral levels and the Figure S8 `pc_RNA` peaks were read from
  the figures by the maintainers.
- No correction notice for the article was found on PubMed or the publisher's
  page as of 2026-11-02.
